newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: China says home-grown grains can feed population.
newsitem.headline: China says home-grown grains can feed population.

text.p: China will be able to achieve self-sufficiency in grain in the coming years, a senior Chinese agriculture official said on Tuesday.

"The Chinese government and people have the ability to solve the problems of grain supply by relying on their own efforts," Liu Zhenwei, deputy director of China's Ministry of Agriculture, said in a paper presented at an Asia-Pacific business forum in Manila.
China's grain demand is expected to rise to 500 million tonnes by 2000 as its population rises to 1.3 billion from 1.2 billion.
By 2030, demand is projected at 640 million tonnes and population numbers at 1.6 billion, Liu said.

"China endeavours to increase its grain production so that self-sufficiency rate of grain under normal conditions will be above 95 percent and the net import rate will not exceed five percent of total consumption," he said.
China produced 490 million tonnes of grain in 1996.
Liu said China hoped to boost production through better farm technology and by increasing the area devoted to agriculture.
China could achieve this if it increased grain yields by one percent from 1996 to 2010 and by 0.7 percent from 2011 to 2030.
Yields currently varied from a low of 3,000-5,000 kg per hectare to 7,500-15,000 kg per hectare.

"In the next few decades China plans to reclaim 300,000 hectares each year to make up for the loss of cultivated land appropriated for non-farming uses and to keep the acreage of cultivated land constant for a longer period of time," he said.
The area sown to grain would be stabilised at about 110 million hectares, Liu added.
